title: Geometry and separable field change of reduced algebraic normalization
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a reduced scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Define $X^
u$ as the disjoint union of the normalizations [def-sc-normalization] of the finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$, with their reduced induced structures, and let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be the canonical map. Then $
u$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The subset $N\subseteq X$ of points whose local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] is a dense open, and $
u^{-1}(N)	o N$ is an isomorphism. For every open subscheme $W\subseteq X$, $
u^{-1}(W)	o W$ is canonically the normalization of $W$. If $K/k$ is a separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (every finitely generated subextension is separably generated), the canonical comparison $(X_K)^
u	o X^
u	imes_k K$ is an isomorphism over $X_K=X	imes_k K$ [def-pc-base-change]; no algebraicity or finiteness of $K/k$ is assumed. In particular this comparison is an isomorphism for every extension of an algebraically closed base field $k$.

source.place: Tags 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), 0C3N (lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields); Morphisms Tags 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), 035K (lemma-normalization-localization), 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components). The normal locus equals the isomorphism locus: on an affine chart Spec A with finite integral closure B, it is the complement of the support of the finite A-module B/A.

proof.text:
The spectrum of a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are 0 and 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ is Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] gives its finitely many components $C_i$ with reduced induced structure. Each $C_i$ is integral and finite type over $k$. Apply [lem-sc-normalization-exists] to $C_i$: $C_i^
u	o C_i$ is finite and surjective. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, the inverse images in these sources are affine with coordinate rings finite over $A/\mathfrak p_i$, hence finite over $A$ using the same generators. Their finite disjoint union is the spectrum of their finite product, a finite $A$-module. Thus $
u$ is finite. Every point belongs to some $C_i$ and has a preimage in $C_i^
u$, so $
u$ is surjective. The empty scheme gives the empty coproduct and satisfies both assertions.

source.place: Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), finiteness and component construction; Morphisms 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components).

proof.text: Fix an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions], $Q(A)$ is the finite product of the fields $\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$ for the minimal primes meeting this chart. By [def-sc-normalization] and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], the component normalizations over this chart have coordinate rings $B_i=\overline{A/\mathfrak p_i}^{\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_i)}$. Thus $\nu^{-1}\operatorname{Spec}A=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=\prod_i B_i\subset Q(A)$. This is exactly the integral closure of $A$ in $Q(A)$: projection of a monic equation proves one inclusion; for a tuple integral in each coordinate, lift the coefficients of its finitely many coordinate monic polynomials to $A$ and multiply them. In each coordinate its own polynomial is a factor, so the resulting monic product annihilates the tuple. This also handles an empty product.

Apply [lem-sbc-integral-closure-finite-normal-product] to $A\to Q(A)$ and the finite product of its component fraction fields (fields are integrally closed domains). It says that every prime localization of $B$ is an integrally closed domain, so $B$ is normal. Choose finite $A$-module generators $b_j$ of $B$ from step 1, write $b_j=a_j/s_j$ in $Q(A)$ with each $s_j$ a nonzerodivisor, and put $s=\prod_j s_j$. Then $sB\subset A$ and $A_s=B_s$. Multiplication by $s$ is injective on $B$, since $B\subset Q(A)$ and $s$ is a unit in $Q(A)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-zerodivisors-union-minimal-primes], $s$ avoids every minimal prime; hence $D(s)$ contains every generic point of the chart and is dense. This gives a dense open over which $\nu$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic); Morphisms 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal); explicit finite-generator denominator argument.

proof.text: For $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] identifies $B_{\mathfrak p}$ with the integral closure of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ in $Q(A)_{\mathfrak p}=Q(A_{\mathfrak p})$. The latter identification follows from [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions]: localization kills precisely the field factors whose minimal primes are not contained in $\mathfrak p$, and keeps the others, exactly the minimal primes of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ by the inclusion-preserving prime correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization]. If $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is an integrally closed domain, this closure is $A_{\mathfrak p}$. Conversely, if $A_{\mathfrak p}=B_{\mathfrak p}$, this local ring is a normal domain: its maximal ideal contracts to a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ and $(B_{\mathfrak p})_{\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak p}}=B_{\mathfrak q}$. A local ring localized at its maximal ideal is itself, and $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a normal domain by step 3. Therefore the normal points of the chart are precisely the primes where $(B/A)_{\mathfrak p}=0$. For generators $m_1,\ldots,m_h$ of $B/A$, vanishing at $\mathfrak p$ means some $u_j\notin\mathfrak p$ kills each $m_j$; their product kills all generators. Consequently these primes form $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(\operatorname{Ann}_A(B/A))$, an open containing $D(s)$ from step 3. On this open the localized inclusion $A\to B$ is an isomorphism. These local descriptions agree on overlaps because they use the intrinsic local ring, so they give the dense open $N$ and $\nu^{-1}(N)\cong N$.

source.place: Morphisms Tags 0C3B (lemma-stalk-normalization) and 035K (lemma-normalization-localization); finite-module annihilator calculation written out.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], a principal open is affine with its coordinate ring the stated localization. For a principal open $D(f)\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] gives $B_f=\overline{A_f}^{Q(A)_f}$. The total-fractions description [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] identifies $Q(A)_f$ with $Q(A_f)$ by discarding the component field factors in which $f=0$. Step 2 applied to $A_f$ therefore identifies $\operatorname{Spec}B_f\to\operatorname{Spec}A_f$ with the normalization. Cover any open $W\subset X$ by such principal opens in affine charts. On a further principal restriction $D(fg)$ both iterated maps send $b/f^n$ to that same fraction in $B_{fg}$; equality can be tested on principal opens inside each overlap. Thus the identifications agree on overlaps and glue canonically to identify $\nu^{-1}(W)\to W$ with the normalization of $W$. Empty opens contribute no charts.

Let $K/k$ be separable in the stated, possibly transcendental, sense. On the above affine chart set $A_K=A\otimes_k K$ and $B_K=B\otimes_k K$. The normal-algebra scalar-extension theorem [lem-weil-pbc-normal-algebra-separable-scalar-extension] applies to the normal $B$ of step 3 and makes $B_K$ normal. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat] and the injectivity characterization in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], tensoring $A\hookrightarrow B$ and multiplication by the nonzerodivisor $s$ preserves injectivity. Thus $A_K\hookrightarrow B_K$, and $s$ is a nonzerodivisor on both rings; the same finite generators show $B_K$ is finite over $A_K$, and $sB_K\subset A_K$. A normal ring is reduced: if a nonzero nilpotent $b$ existed, choose a maximal ideal containing its proper annihilator; then $b/1$ would be a nonzero nilpotent in a domain localization, a contradiction. Hence $B_K$, and its subring $A_K$, are reduced. Both are finite-type $K$-algebras and therefore Noetherian by the affine instance of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

The inclusion $B_K\subset (A_K)_s\subset Q(A_K)$ is injective because $s$ is a nonzerodivisor on $B_K$ and $sB_K\subset A_K$. It identifies $Q(B_K)$ with $Q(A_K)$ explicitly: a nonzerodivisor $a$ of $A_K$ is one on $B_K$, since $ab=0$ implies $a(sb)=0$ in $A_K$, hence $sb=0$ and $b=0$. Conversely, if $t$ is a nonzerodivisor of $B_K$, then $st\in A_K$ is a nonzerodivisor there, and a fraction $b/t$ equals $(sb)/(st)$ in $Q(A_K)$. The Noetherian ring $B_K$ has finitely many minimal primes by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions] to the reduced Noetherian ring $B_K$: its normality makes it integrally closed in this common total fraction ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], every element of $B_K$ is integral over $A_K$. Any element of $Q(A_K)$ integral over $A_K$ is also integral over $B_K$ (the same monic equation), hence belongs to $B_K$. Therefore $B_K$ is exactly the integral closure of $A_K$ in $Q(A_K)$. By step 2 this identifies $\operatorname{Spec}B_K$ with the normalization of $\operatorname{Spec}A_K$. To identify the canonical comparison, flatness as in step 6 preserves injectivity of multiplication by every nonzerodivisor $a$ of $A$, so $A\to A_K$ extends uniquely to $\iota:Q(A)\to Q(A_K)$, $x/a\mapsto (x\otimes1)/(a\otimes1)$. The comparison is Spec of the ring isomorphism $B_K\to\overline{A_K}^{Q(A_K)}$, $b\otimes c\mapsto c\iota(b)$. On restriction to $D(f)$ this sends $(b/f^n)\otimes c$ to $c\iota(b)/\iota(f)^n$; on any further principal restriction both composites have this formula. Principal opens inside affine overlaps cover those overlaps, so these local maps agree and glue to the canonical comparison over $X_K$.

proof.text: If $k$ is algebraically closed and $K/k$ is arbitrary, take any finitely generated subextension $L/k$. The Mathlib field tool [lem-weil-pbc-algclosed-fg-field-separating-basis] supplies a finite transcendence basis with separable algebraic remainder. Thus each such $L/k$ is separably generated, exactly condition (2) of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. So $K/k$ satisfies the hypothesis of steps 6 and 7, giving the stated special case without assuming that $K/k$ is algebraic or finite.
